questions.prompt: Which of the following is required by scrum?
options: Release planning
Sprint retrospective
Sprint burndown chart
Developers must stand-up at the daily scrum
All of the above
questions.explanation: The Sprint Retrospective is a Scrum event. Release planning and burndowns can be useful practices, but Scrum does not require them. Standing at the Daily Scrum is not a rule.
answerText: Sprint retrospective

questions.prompt: An Increment must be released to customers or users at the end of each sprint?
options: True
False
questions.explanation: A usable Increment must meet the Definition of Done. Release may happen before the Sprint ends; releasing every Sprint is not mandatory. The Sprint Review is not a release gate.
answerText: False

questions.prompt: When should a Sprint Goal be created?
options: It should have been created in the previous Sprint during Product Backlog refinement.
It must be established before Sprint Planning in order to begin planning.
A Sprint Goal is not mandatory in Scrum.
At any time during the Sprint.
During Sprint Planning.
questions.explanation: The whole Scrum Team collaborates on the Sprint Goal during Sprint Planning. Finalize it before Planning ends, not sometime later in the Sprint.
answerText: During Sprint Planning.

questions.prompt: What are three benefits of self-management?
options: Increased self-accountability
Increased accuracy of estimates
Increased commitment
Increased creativity
Increased rule compliance
questions.explanation: Self-management lets people decide who does what, when and how. The key associates this with accountability, commitment and creativity; it does not guarantee precise estimates or rule compliance.
answerText: Increased self-accountability
Increased commitment
Increased creativity

questions.prompt: A project manager working with your scrum team has raised concerns about progress and money spent. What are the 2 best responses?
options: Have a discussion with the project manager, share the current impediments and forecast for the sprint.
Share the last stakeholders briefing document prepared by the product owner.
Promote transparency by sharing the Product Backlog and ensuring the project manager has access.
Scrum does not have project managers so disregards their concerns
Show the earned value analysis
questions.explanation: Make current work and uncertainty transparent, and discuss the forecast and impediments. A job title outside the Scrum Team is not a reason to dismiss a stakeholder's concerns.
answerText: Have a discussion with the project manager, share the current impediments and forecast for the sprint.
Promote transparency by sharing the Product Backlog and ensuring the project manager has access.

questions.prompt: When does a developer take ownership of a Sprint Backlog item of value?
options: At the Sprint planning event.
During the Daily Scrum.
Never. All Sprint Backlog Items are “owned” by the entire Scrum Team
Whenever a team member can accommodate more work.
questions.explanation: Avoid treating a valuable outcome as one person's isolated responsibility. The whole Scrum Team creates a useful Increment; specifically, the Sprint Backlog is a plan by and for the Developers. The mock's ownership wording is imprecise.
answerText: Never. All Sprint Backlog Items are “owned” by the entire Scrum Team

questions.prompt: When is a Sprint over?
options: When the Product Owner says it is done.
When all Product Backlog items meet their definition of “Done”.
When all the tasks are completed.
When the time-box expires.
questions.explanation: A Sprint ends when its fixed timebox expires; it is not extended to finish work. Separately, only the Product Owner may cancel a Sprint if its goal becomes obsolete.
answerText: When the time-box expires.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes Scrum?
options: A framework to generate value through adaptive solutions for complex problems
A complete methodology that defines how to develop software
A cookbook that defines best practices for software development
A defined and predictive process that conforms to the principles of Scientific Management
questions.explanation: Scrum is a lightweight framework for adaptive solutions to complex problems. It does not prescribe every engineering practice or a complete software methodology.
answerText: A framework to generate value through adaptive solutions for complex problems

questions.prompt: Which two ways of creating scrum teams are consistent with scrum's values?
options: Managers personally re-assign current subordinates to new teams
Bring all the people together and let them organize into scrum teams
Managers collaborate to assign individuals to specific teams
The chief product owner determines the new team structures and assignments
Existing teams propose how they would like to go about organizing into the new structure
questions.explanation: Invite people to organize and propose team structures. This supports self-management and respect. Managers assigning everyone unilaterally is weaker than enabling the people doing the work.
answerText: Bring all the people together and let them organize into scrum teams
Existing teams propose how they would like to go about organizing into the new structure

questions.prompt: Which two things are appropriate for a Scrum Master to do if Scrum Team doesn’t have the tools and environment to completely finish each selected Product Backlog item?
options: Coach the Scrum Team to improve its skills, tools, and environment over time and adjust the Definition of "Done" accordingly.
Encourage the Product Owner to accept partially "Done" increments until the situation improves.
Refocus the current Sprint on establishing the Scrum Team’s environment instead of delivering an increment.
Declare the Scrum Team not ready for Scrum.
Have the scrum Team establish a Definition of "Done" that is actually possible to achieve given current circumstances.
questions.explanation: The mock key selects coaching and an achievable Definition of Done. Missing capability must be addressed without lowering organizational minimum quality standards or decreasing quality during the Sprint. Partial work is not a Done Increment.
answerText: Coach the Scrum Team to improve its skills, tools, and environment over time and adjust the Definition of "Done" accordingly.
Have the scrum Team establish a Definition of "Done" that is actually possible to achieve given current circumstances.

questions.prompt:
The Scrum Team has been working on a product for nine Sprints. A new product owner who is new to scrum joins the team and understands she is accountable for the product backlog. However she is unsure about the purpose of the product backlog. She has read that the product backlog should be a list of all user features for the product.  She goes to the scrum master asking where to put the other types of requirements that are going to be taken into account. Are all of the following types of requirement acceptable on the product backlog?
Stability requirements
Performance requirements
Product functionality
Documentation
Fixes
options: Yes, they all belong on the product backlog. The Product backlog is supposed to be the single source of truth for all the work for the product.

No, Product Backlog is a tool for the product owner. The product owner represents the users and stakeholders. Other types of requirement should be managed separately by the developers. They are not the product owner’s concern.
questions.explanation: The Product Backlog can contain functionality, fixes, documentation and quality-related work. It is the single source of work for the Scrum Team; it is not limited to user-facing features.
answerText: Yes, they all belong on the product backlog. The Product backlog is supposed to be the single source of truth for all the work for the product.

questions.prompt: Which topics should be discussed in the Sprint review?
options: The scrum process and how it was used during the sprint
Coding and engineering practices
The product increment
All of the above
questions.explanation: Of these choices, the product Increment is the best answer. The Review also examines progress toward the Product Goal, changes in the environment and what to do next. It is more than a demo.
answerText: The product increment

questions.prompt: Who is accountable for tracking the remaining work of a sprint?
options: The project Manager
The product owner
The scrum master
The Developers
questions.explanation: Developers maintain and adapt their Sprint Backlog and inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal. The Daily Scrum is not a status report to a project manager.
answerText: The Developers

questions.prompt: True or false: Sprint reviews are an opportunity to collect customer feedback
options: True
False
questions.explanation: The Scrum Team and stakeholders inspect outcomes and determine adaptations. Customer feedback can inform the next Product Backlog decisions.
answerText: True

questions.prompt: Which approach is best for Scrum Teams in order to produce valuable increments?
options: Each Scrum Team works on an independent set of components
Each Scrum Member works only as an independent layer of the system
Each developer works on the component where they feel that they can contribute
Each Scrum Teams is accountable for developing functionality from beginning to end
questions.explanation: Cross-functional teams can deliver an integrated, usable result end to end. Component or layer silos create dependencies and do not alone ensure a valuable Increment.
answerText: Each Scrum Teams is accountable for developing functionality from beginning to end

questions.prompt: When is a product backlog item considered complete?
options: When the item passes all acceptance criteria
When the item has gained product sponsor approval
At the end of the sprint
When the item meets the definition of done
questions.explanation: A Product Backlog item becomes part of an Increment when it meets the Definition of Done. Acceptance criteria or sponsor approval alone do not replace that quality standard.
answerText: When the item meets the definition of done

questions.prompt: The definition of Done serves which three purposes?
options: Guide the Developers on how many Product Backlog items to select for the Sprint.
Create a shared understanding of when work is complete.
Describe the purpose, objective, and time-box of each Scrum event.
Describe the work that must be done before the Sprint is allowed to end.
Increase transparency.
questions.explanation: Done gives a shared understanding of completion and transparency. Developers also use it with capacity and past performance when forecasting what they can complete. A Sprint's end is set by time, not completion.
answerText: Guide the Developers on how many Product Backlog items to select for the Sprint.
Create a shared understanding of when work is complete.
Increase transparency.

questions.prompt: You are the scrum master for four scrum teams working from the same product backlog. Several developers come to you complaining that work identified for the upcoming sprints will require full-time commitment from a specialist who is external to the teams. What should the scrum master consider in this situation?
options: The ability of the scrum teams to produce integrated increments
The desire to maintain stable velocity
The need to have enough work to keep all Developers busy
The benefit of developers figuring out a solution for themselves
questions.explanation: Consider whether teams can create an integrated usable Increment, and coach their ability to resolve dependencies themselves. Keeping everyone busy or maintaining velocity is not the objective.
answerText: The ability of the scrum teams to produce integrated increments
The benefit of developers figuring out a solution for themselves

questions.prompt: Who must attend the daily Scrum?
options: The Developers and the Product Owner
The developers
The Developers and the Scrum Master
The Scrum Master and the product Owner
The scrum Team
questions.explanation: The Daily Scrum is for Developers. A Product Owner or Scrum Master working on Sprint Backlog items participates as a Developer, not because their separate accountability requires attendance.
answerText: The developers

questions.prompt: Which three questions might be answered by Developers at the Daily Scrum?
options: How is the Sprint proceeding?
What did I do yesterday that helped the Development Team meet the Sprint Goal?
Why were you late?
What will I do today to help the Scrum Team meet the Sprint Goal?
How many hours did I spend on the project yesterday?
What will I be working on tomorrow?
Do I see any impediment that prevents me or the Developers from meeting the Sprint Goal?
questions.explanation: The question says “might”: yesterday, today and impediments are possible prompts. They are not prescribed by the 2020 Guide. Developers choose the structure, provided it focuses on progress toward the Sprint Goal and creates an actionable plan.
answerText: What did I do yesterday that helped the Development Team meet the Sprint Goal?
What will I do today to help the Scrum Team meet the Sprint Goal?
Do I see any impediment that prevents me or the Developers from meeting the Sprint Goal?

questions.prompt: Which of the following are true about the length of the Sprint?
options: The length of the Sprint should be proportional to the work that is done in between Sprints.
Sprint length is determined during Sprint Planning, and should hold the time it will take to code the planned features in the upcoming Sprint, but does not include time for any testing.
Sprint length is determined during Sprint Planning, and should be long enough to make sure the Scrum Team can deliver what is to be accomplished in the upcoming Sprint.
All Sprints must be one month or less.
questions.explanation: A Sprint is one month or less. Testing and other work needed for a Done Increment belong inside the Sprint; timeboxes are not extended to fit a forecast.
answerText: All Sprints must be one month or less.

questions.prompt: When developers are having trouble delivering an increment because they do not understand a functional requirement, what should they do?
options: Partially complete the functionality, and discuss the remaining work and the sprint review
Add a specialist to the Development Team
Collaborate with the product owner to determine what is possible and acceptable
Defer the work to a more appropriate sprint
questions.explanation: Clarify the requirement with the Product Owner and negotiate scope while protecting the Sprint Goal. Do not silently deliver partial work or defer work without collaboration.
answerText: Collaborate with the product owner to determine what is possible and acceptable

questions.prompt: Every scrum team should have
options: One lead developer and no more than 8 other members
The competencies and skills needed it to deliver an increment in a sprint
At least one representative from each major department such as quality assurance, development and marketing
questions.explanation: The team collectively needs the skills to deliver value each Sprint. Scrum does not require a lead developer or one representative from every department.
answerText: The competencies and skills needed it to deliver an increment in a sprint

questions.prompt: True or false: A product owner is essentially the same thing as a traditional project manager
options: True
False
questions.explanation: The Product Owner focuses on maximizing product value and effective Product Backlog management. Scrum does not define that accountability as a traditional project manager.
answerText: False

questions.prompt: What are the two primary ways a scrum master helps a scrum team work at its highest level of productivity?
options: By keeping high value features high in the product backlog
By ensuring the meetings start and end at the proper time
By removing impediments that hinder the scrum team
By facilitating scrum team decision
questions.explanation: The Scrum Master enables effectiveness, causes impediments to be removed, and coaches self-management. Facilitating decisions can help; they do not take over Product Backlog ordering.
answerText: By removing impediments that hinder the scrum team
By facilitating scrum team decision

questions.prompt: What does it mean for a scrum team to be cross-functional?
options: The scrum team not only includes developers, but also, business analyst, architects, and testers
The scrum team includes cross-skilled individuals who are able to contribute to do what is necessary to deliver an increment.
Developers on the Scrum Team work closely with the business analyst, the architects, developers and testers who are not on the team
The scrum team are a virtual team drawing from separate teams of business analyst, architects, developers and testers
questions.explanation: Cross-functionality means the team collectively has the skills needed to create value. It does not require every person to master every skill, and it does not mean relying on external functional silos.
answerText: The scrum team includes cross-skilled individuals who are able to contribute to do what is necessary to deliver an increment.

questions.prompt: You are a product owner with a proven track record in your company. Your management has asked you to take the lead in the development of new product. Four teams new to scrum will build this product. You have gathered a number of requirements and ideas into an early form of product backlog. How would you minimize dependencies between the scrum teams?
options: You work with the Developers on how the best analyse and break apart the work
You create an independent Product Backlog per Scrum Team
You identify the dependencies and reorder the product backlog for them
You raise this as an impediment with the scrum master
You divide product backlog items among the four product owners
questions.explanation: Collaborate with Developers to analyze and split work in ways that reduce dependencies. Teams working on one product share a Product Backlog and Product Owner.
answerText: You work with the Developers on how the best analyse and break apart the work

questions.prompt: A Product Owner can measure the success of the delivered value by an increase in the team’s velocity?
options: True
False
questions.explanation: Velocity describes estimated work completed. It does not establish better customer outcomes or realized product value.
answerText: False

questions.prompt: A Product Owner with multiple teams working on one product should maintain separate Product Backlogs for each team?
options: True
False
questions.explanation: Teams focused on the same product share the Product Goal, Product Backlog and Product Owner. Separate team backlogs would fragment product ordering and transparency.
answerText: False

questions.prompt: In accordance with Scrum theory, how should a group of 25 people be divided into multiple scrum teams
options: Check with the allocation department to see who has worked together before and make these the first teams
Create a matrix of skills, seniority, and level of experience to assign people to teams
It doesn't really matter since you can rotate the team every Sprint to spread knowledge
Understanding the product, the product vision and the rule of the scrum framework, the people divide themselves into teams
questions.explanation: Help people understand the product, direction and Scrum, then enable them to organize. Self-management is more consistent than allocating people solely through a management matrix.
answerText: Understanding the product, the product vision and the rule of the scrum framework, the people divide themselves into teams

questions.prompt: What is the responsibility of the Product Owner in crafting the sprint goal?
options: The Product Owner has no responsibility in it. This is the developers’ responsibility.
The Product Owner should not come to the sprint planning without a clearly defined Sprint Goal.
The Product Owner defines the scope for a sprint and therefore also the sprint goal.
The Product Owner should come to the sprint planning with a business objective in mind and work with the developers to craft the sprint goal based upon the forecast.
The Product Owner must work with the stakeholders to set each Sprint’s goal.
questions.explanation: The Product Owner proposes how the Sprint could increase value. The whole Scrum Team collaborates to craft the Sprint Goal. The Product Owner does not impose it alone.
answerText: The Product Owner should come to the sprint planning with a business objective in mind and work with the developers to craft the sprint goal based upon the forecast.

questions.prompt: Product Owners must create alone clear and unambiguous acceptance criteria for each product backlog item before it may be selected in Sprint planning?
options: True
False
questions.explanation: The Product Owner may delegate backlog work and collaborate with others. Scrum does not mandate a complete set of acceptance criteria written alone before selection.
answerText: False

questions.prompt: What might indicate to a Product Owner that she needs to work more with the Scrum Team?
options: She isn’t working full time with the Scrum Team
The acceptance tests don’t appear to be complete
People leave the team
The increment presented at the Sprint Review does not reflect what she thought she has asked for
questions.explanation: A mismatch between the expected and actual Increment suggests a need for better collaboration and shared understanding. Scrum prescribes no fixed percentage of Product Owner attendance.
answerText: The increment presented at the Sprint Review does not reflect what she thought she has asked for

questions.prompt: Why would you expect a product owner to care about the Scrum team adhering to its Definition of done?
options: The definition of done can affect the product’s total cost of ownership
The product owner should not care about the definition of Done, it is the scrum Team’s responsibility
To forecast the team’s productivity over time
To have complete transparency into what has been done at the end of each sprint
To be able to punish the team when they do not meet their velocity goal for the sprint
questions.explanation: Done exposes the actual state of the product and affects quality-related cost and risk. It supports meaningful inspection; it is not a tool for punishing a velocity miss.
answerText: The definition of done can affect the product’s total cost of ownership
To have complete transparency into what has been done at the end of each sprint

questions.prompt: During the Sprint Review it is up to the stakeholders to reorder the Product Backlog?
options: True
False
questions.explanation: Stakeholders collaborate at the Review and can influence priorities. The Product Owner remains accountable for Product Backlog ordering; the stakeholders do not take over that accountability.
answerText: False

questions.prompt: In the middle of the sprint, the customer decides that there are two new features she wants. The product owner could:
options: Introduce these features at the next Daily Scrum
Ask the Developers to consider whether they can add these features in the current sprint
Have the Scrum Master add these features to the current Sprint
Add the features to the product Backlog
questions.explanation: New requests can enter the Product Backlog. Developers and the Product Owner may discuss changes within the current Sprint, provided they do not endanger the Sprint Goal or decrease quality.
answerText: Ask the Developers to consider whether they can add these features in the current sprint
Add the features to the product Backlog

questions.prompt: What is a product owner typically responsible for during a sprint
options: Updating the work plan for the developers on a daily basis
Collaborating with stakeholders, users Communities and project managers
Attending every daily Scrum to answer questions about the sprint backlog items
Nothing
Working with the scrum team on Product backlog refinement
Creating Financial Reporting upon the spend hours reported by the developers
questions.explanation: The Product Owner collaborates with stakeholders and with the Scrum Team on the Product Backlog. Developers own their daily plan; the Product Owner need not attend every Daily Scrum.
answerText: Collaborating with stakeholders, users Communities and project managers
Working with the scrum team on Product backlog refinement

questions.prompt: What typically happens if the product owner is not sufficiently clear at the sprint planning?
options: The Developers has difficulties creating a forecast of work for a Sprint.
Nothing in particular.
It’s acceptable if the Product Owner can give the scrum team a clear Sprint Goal.
Sprint Planning is canceled so refinement can be done first.
The scrum master shouldn’t allow this it happen. Look for new scrum master and restart the sprint.
questions.explanation: Unclear priorities or items make the Developers' forecast harder. Planning requires enough shared understanding of the goal, selected work and how to deliver it.
answerText: The Developers has difficulties creating a forecast of work for a Sprint.

questions.prompt: If product backlog refinement is needed, when should the product backlog be refined and who should participate?
options: The scrum team does it in the actual sprint if they have not been able to do it in proceeding sprints
Business Analysis in the organization should do this work for the scrum Team, 1-2 sprints ahead of the development sprints
The Product Owner takes the time between the sprints to do it
The Product Owner must do this as essential work in sprint 0
The scrum team in the preceding one or two Sprints
questions.explanation: Refinement is ongoing work within Sprints and can prepare items for future Sprints. There is no mandated one- or two-Sprint horizon, separate Sprint 0, or gap between Sprints.
answerText: The scrum team does it in the actual sprint if they have not been able to do it in proceeding sprints
The scrum team in the preceding one or two Sprints

questions.prompt: How much of the sprint backlog must be defined during the sprint planning event?
options: Just enough to understand design and architectural implications
Enough so the developers can create their forecast of what work they can do
The entire Sprint backlog must be identified and estimated by the end of Sprint planning
Just enough tasks for the scrum master to be confident in the developers understanding of the sprint
questions.explanation: Create enough of a plan to support a credible forecast and start work. The Sprint Backlog emerges and is updated during the Sprint; every task need not be known upfront.
answerText: Enough so the developers can create their forecast of what work they can do

questions.prompt: The value delivered by a product can only be determined by revenue.
options: True.
False.
questions.explanation: Revenue is one signal. Customer experience, satisfaction and product use can also inform value decisions; Scrum specifies no single metric.
answerText: False.

questions.prompt: Which metrics will help a Product Owner establish that the value is being delivered.
options: Time to market
Scope implemented
Velocity.
Productivity.
Budget spent.
questions.explanation: Time to market reflects delivery capability; scope implemented reflects output. Neither alone establishes realized customer value. The supplied key is unreliable as proof of value: examine customer outcomes alongside these measures.
answerText: Time to market
Scope implemented

questions.prompt: The daily scrum is an event that happens every day what would be 3 key concerns if this frequency were to be lowered to every 2 or 3 days?
options: Opportunities to inspect and adapt the sprint backlog are lost
The scrum master loses the ability to update the gantt chart properly
Too much work is spent updating the Scrum board before the meeting
The Sprint Backlog may become inaccurate
Impediments are raised and resolved more slowly
The product owner cannot accurately report progress to the stakeholders
questions.explanation: Reducing the Daily Scrum frequency loses regular opportunities to inspect and adapt, can leave the plan stale, and can delay surfacing impediments. It is a 15-minute event every working day.
answerText: Opportunities to inspect and adapt the sprint backlog are lost
The Sprint Backlog may become inaccurate
Impediments are raised and resolved more slowly

questions.prompt: True or False: Product Owners must specify complete acceptance criteria for a Product Backlog item before the team can select the item in Sprint Planning
options: True
False
questions.explanation: An item must be sufficiently understood and small enough to be Done in a Sprint. Scrum does not require exhaustive acceptance criteria before selection or a separate approval gate.
answerText: False

questions.prompt: How should a Scrum Team deal with non-functional requirements?
options: Ensure every Increment meets them
Manage them during the integration Sprint prior to the Release Sprint
Make sure the release department understands these requirements, but it is not the Scrum Team’s responsibility
Assign them to the lead developers on the team
questions.explanation: Each Increment must meet applicable quality standards. Put product-wide quality measures in the Definition of Done and represent additional product work in the backlog. Do not postpone required quality to a separate release Sprint.
answerText: Ensure every Increment meets them

questions.prompt: The Developers find out during the sprint that they aren't likely to build everything they forecasted. What would you expect a Product Owner to do?
options: Cancel the sprint.
Change the Sprint Goal.
Re-work the selected product backlog items with the Developers to meet the Sprint Goal.
Skip Product Backlog refinement activities.
Inform management that more resources are needed.
questions.explanation: Re-negotiate the selected work with Developers while preserving the Sprint Goal. A missed forecast alone is not a reason to change the goal, cut quality or cancel the Sprint.
answerText: Re-work the selected product backlog items with the Developers to meet the Sprint Goal.

questions.prompt: Why is it important that there is only one product owner per product?
options: The scrum team always knows who determines the order of the product backlog
It is clear who is accountable for the ultimate success of the product
It helps avoid barriers to effective communication and rapid decision making
The scrum master knows who will be his/her back up whenever he goes on vacation
It would confuse the stakeholders if they had to work with more than one person
questions.explanation: One Product Owner makes ordering accountability and value decisions clear. They remain one person even when representing many stakeholders. The whole Scrum Team still creates the Increment.
answerText: The scrum team always knows who determines the order of the product backlog
It is clear who is accountable for the ultimate success of the product
It helps avoid barriers to effective communication and rapid decision making

questions.prompt: My job as Product Owner focuses on the following
options: Working with the customers and the stakeholders to identify the most important requirements
Being with the scrum team all the time, just in case they need me to clarify a requirement
Clearly communicating project or release status and strategies to customers and stakeholders
Writing clear transparent user stories
questions.explanation: Understand stakeholder needs and communicate product direction and progress. Scrum does not require user stories as the item format, or constant physical attendance.
answerText: Working with the customers and the stakeholders to identify the most important requirements
Clearly communicating project or release status and strategies to customers and stakeholders

questions.prompt: Dependencies could influence how the product owner orders product backlog items
options: True
False
questions.explanation: Dependencies can affect a useful order, alongside value, risk and goals. Product Backlog ordering is a judgment about effective product progress, not a rigid ranking formula.
answerText: True

questions.prompt: The product owner is the person who will be held accountable if a product does not achieve its goals or deliver value. Does this mean that the Product Owner has the final say over the definition of DONE?
options: Yes. The product owner decides the definition of “done”. The development team may be consulted.
No. The Scrum Team decides the definition of “done”. The product owner should be consulted.
questions.explanation: Organizational Definition of Done standards apply as a minimum. If none exist, the Scrum Team creates a suitable Definition of Done. The Product Owner participates as part of that team, without unilateral final authority.
answerText: No. The Scrum Team decides the definition of “done”. The product owner should be consulted.

questions.prompt: The cone of uncertainty can be used to do what?
options: Determine the cost of a project before it is begun.
Project what will complete by a given Sprint.
Determine whether to cut quality, similar to the "Iron Triangle" of Software Development.
Illustrate that, as a forecast lengthens, it is increasingly less certain.
questions.explanation: Longer forecast horizons usually involve more uncertainty. The Guide requires empirical forecasting but does not define a cone of uncertainty. Treat this as a supplementary forecasting concept, not a Scrum artifact.
answerText: Illustrate that, as a forecast lengthens, it is increasingly less certain.

questions.prompt: In order to maximize the value of the product, a product owner needs awareness of the following:
options: Competitive research
Customer feedback
Product vision
Forecasting & feasibility
All of the above
None of the above
questions.explanation: Customer feedback, competitive context, product direction and feasibility can inform value decisions. No single input is sufficient; validate assumptions with evidence. This is product-management application beyond the Guide's detailed rules.
answerText: All of the above

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of a Sprint Review?
options: To build team spirit
To take time to judge the validity of the project
To review the Scrum Team’s activities and processes during the sprint
To inspect the product increment with the stakeholders and collect feedback on the next steps
questions.explanation: Inspect the Sprint outcome with stakeholders, discuss progress toward the Product Goal and determine adaptations. The Retrospective focuses on quality and team effectiveness instead.
answerText: To inspect the product increment with the stakeholders and collect feedback on the next steps

questions.prompt: Why does a Developers need a sprint goal?
options: Sprint Goals are not valuable. Everything is known from the Product Backlog.
A Sprint Goal only gives purpose to Sprint 0.
The Developers are more focused with a common yet specific goal.
A sprint Goal ensures that all of the Product Backlog items selected for the Sprint are implemented
questions.explanation: The Sprint Goal creates a shared purpose and focus. It allows flexibility in exact scope; it does not guarantee completion of every selected item.
answerText: The Developers are more focused with a common yet specific goal.

questions.prompt: All planned activities for the product done by the Scrum team are inside the product Backlog?
options: True
False
questions.explanation: The Guide calls the Product Backlog the single source of work. The detailed Sprint delivery plan lives in the Sprint Backlog, so not every task or event must be separately listed in the Product Backlog. The mock's wording does not distinguish these meanings.
answerText: False

questions.prompt: How often should customer satisfaction be measured?
options: Quarterly
Frequently
Daily
Annually
questions.explanation: Frequent customer feedback supports inspection and adaptation. Scrum does not mandate a fixed customer-satisfaction survey schedule. Use a cadence that supports useful decisions.
answerText: Frequently

questions.prompt: A product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product that is the result of the work of the Scrum Team. Which of the following can be delegated to others, while the product Owner remains accountable for the work?
options: Attending the Sprint Review
Creating the Sprint Goal
Developing and communicating the Product Goal
Ordering the Product Backlog
questions.explanation: Developing and communicating the Product Goal and ordering the Product Backlog can be delegated. The Product Owner retains accountability for effective Product Backlog management.
answerText: Developing and communicating the Product Goal
Ordering the Product Backlog

questions.prompt: Which best describes the product backlog?
options: It is baselined to follow change management processes
It provides just enough information to enable a scrum team to start the design phase of a product
It is allowed to grow and change as more is learned about the product and its customers
It contains all foreseeable tasks and requirements from which the scrum team can develop and maintain a complete project plan
questions.explanation: The Product Backlog is emergent: it changes as more is learned. It is not a frozen requirements baseline or an exhaustive prediction of all future work.
answerText: It is allowed to grow and change as more is learned about the product and its customers

questions.prompt: Scrum is based on empiricism. All Scrum artifacts must be transparent to ensure sufficient accuracy of inspection. Which two measures ensures that the product backlog is transparent?.
options: The product Backlog is ordered.
The product Backlog only has work for the next 2 sprints.
The product Backlog is managed using a web-based tool.
The product Backlog is available to all stakeholders
Each Product Backlog item has a MoSCoW priority
questions.explanation: An ordered, visible and understood backlog supports transparency. Scrum does not prescribe a particular software tool, point scale, MoSCoW scheme or two-Sprint-only limit.
answerText: The product Backlog is ordered.
The product Backlog is available to all stakeholders

questions.prompt: Which is NOT a valid consideration when ordering a Product Backlog
options: Alignment with business strategy and goal
Importance to customers
Risk
Development teams tools & techniques
Dependencies on other product backlog items
questions.explanation: The key rejects Developers' tools and techniques as an ordering criterion. The Product Owner should not dictate technical implementation, but technical constraints can legitimately influence feasibility, risk and ordering. The absolute wording is unreliable.
answerText: Development teams tools & techniques

questions.prompt: The scrum Team is accountable for making available the most valuable product?
options: True
False
questions.explanation: The whole Scrum Team is accountable for a valuable, useful Increment every Sprint. The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing product value. The mock's wording about the most valuable product blurs this distinction.
answerText: True

questions.prompt: Scrum is based on empiricism. All Scrum its artifacts must be transparent to ensure sufficient accuracy of inspection. How can the scrum Team maintain the product Backlog to maximize its  transparency?.
options: A product Backlog items should hold no more than 8 points of work, which is the average in the range of acceptable sizes of 1,2,3,5,8 and 13
The product Backlog is only updated at a release planning meeting with the stakeholders and the change control board present
Product Backlog items must be sized such that the highest ordered items are no bigger than a Sprint
The product Backlog is continually kept up to date with the most recent insights
The product Backlog is only updated at the Sprint Review when both the Scrum Team and the stakeholders are available.
questions.explanation: Keep the Product Backlog current with new insights, visible and understood. Updates are not restricted to a specific meeting and Scrum mandates no particular story-point scale.
answerText: The product Backlog is continually kept up to date with the most recent insights

questions.prompt: True or False: The product Owner should have a complete and exhaustive Product Backlog before the first Sprint Can Start?
options: True
False
questions.explanation: The Product Backlog is emergent. You need sufficient clarity to begin and adapt, not an exhaustive specification of the entire product before the first Sprint.
answerText: False

questions.prompt: What is the accountability of the Product Owner during Sprint 0?
options: Create the overall release plan to ensure that organizational goals are met
There is no such thing as Sprint 0
Make sure enough Product Backlog items are refined to fill the first 3 sprints
Determine the composition of the scrum Team to meet the release plan
Gathering, eliciting and analyzing the requirements to build the Product
questions.explanation: Scrum defines Sprints that produce useful Increments. It does not define a special Sprint 0 exempt from the framework or a mandatory preparatory release-planning phase.
answerText: There is no such thing as Sprint 0

questions.prompt: Which of the following criteria to order Product Backlog items?
options: Value of product backlog items.
Dependencies between product backlog items.
Dependencies to other products.
The availability of the scrum master
All of the above.
questions.explanation: Value and dependencies within or across products can affect ordering. The Scrum Master's availability is not a general basis for selecting the most valuable product work.
answerText: Value of product backlog items.
Dependencies between product backlog items.
Dependencies to other products.

questions.prompt: How much time must a product owner spend with the developers?
options: 40%, or more if the stakeholders agree
Enough so that the product owner is not surprised by the value delivered by the increment
As much time the developers asks the product owner to be present
questions.explanation: The key selects as much time as Developers request, but the Guide gives no fixed allocation or requirement to meet every presence request. Collaborate enough to create shared understanding and enable value decisions; balance stakeholder and team needs.
answerText: As much time the developers asks the product owner to be present

questions.prompt: Who create the Definition of Done
options: The Scrum Master
The developers
The product Owner
The Scrum Team
questions.explanation: The Scrum Team creates the Definition of Done when there is no organizational standard. Existing organizational standards are a minimum; teams sharing a product must comply with the same Definition of Done.
answerText: The Scrum Team

questions.prompt: The product owner must write all the product backlog items (eg: users stories, nonfunctional requirements, etc..) on the product backlog before handing them over to the Scrum Team.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: The Product Owner is accountable for backlog management but may delegate the work. There is no requirement to write all items first or hand them over in a separate phase.
answerText: False

questions.prompt: When should the product owner update the project plan?
options: The product Backlog is the plan in Scrum. It is updated as new information and insights emerge.
Before the sprint planning to know how much work will have to be done in the Sprint.
After the daily scrum to ensure an accurate daily overview of project progress.
Scrum forbids having a project plan.
It is work for the Project Manager.
questions.explanation: Adapt the Product Backlog as new information emerges. It expresses product work; the Sprint Backlog contains the Developers' delivery plan. Scrum neither requires nor forbids additional useful planning tools.
answerText: The product Backlog is the plan in Scrum. It is updated as new information and insights emerge.

questions.prompt: What are 3 advantages of a Product Owner with a solid Product Goal?
options: It helps the Scrum Teams keep focus and they can check any decision against it
It helps the Scrum Teams maintains focus on when the complete Product Backlog should be finished
It is not mandatory in Scrum. There is no real advantage
It is easier to inspect incremental progress at the Sprint Review
It gives a good overall direction so Sprint will feel less like isolated pieces of work
questions.explanation: A Product Goal provides direction, decision focus and a target for inspecting progress. It is not a promise to finish every item that ever enters the Product Backlog.
answerText: It helps the Scrum Teams keep focus and they can check any decision against it
It is easier to inspect incremental progress at the Sprint Review
It gives a good overall direction so Sprint will feel less like isolated pieces of work

questions.prompt: The Product Owner makes sure the right stakeholders are invited to the Sprint Retrospective. They might have important instructions for team improvements.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: The Retrospective is the Scrum Team's opportunity to improve quality and effectiveness. Inviting stakeholders to issue instructions is not the Product Owner's prescribed responsibility. Stakeholder collaboration is central to the Sprint Review.
answerText: False

questions.prompt: You are the Scrum Master of a new to be developed Product. Development is going to require 45 people. What is a good first question for you to suggest the group thinks about when forming into teams?
options: Who are going to be the team leads?
How will we make sure all teams have the right amount of expertise?
Who are the subject matter experts on each team?
What is the right mixture of senior and junior people on each team?
questions.explanation: Start by ensuring teams collectively have the skills to create value. Scrum does not require team leads or a fixed senior/junior staffing formula.
answerText: How will we make sure all teams have the right amount of expertise?

questions.prompt: How much time is required after a sprint to prepare the next sprint?
options: The break between Sprints is timeboxed to 1 week for 1 month sprint, and usually less for shorter sprints
None. A sprint starts immediately following the end of the previous sprint.
Enough time for the requirements for the next Sprint to be determined and documented
Enough time for the developers to finish the testing from the last sprint
All of the above
questions.explanation: The next Sprint starts immediately after the previous Sprint ends. Refinement, planning, testing and other work happen within Sprints; there is no mandatory between-Sprint preparation period.
answerText: None. A sprint starts immediately following the end of the previous sprint.

questions.prompt: A new developer is having continuing conflicts with existing developers on the scrum team and which is impacting the delivery of the increment. If necessary, who is responsible for removing the Developer?
options: The scrum team is accountable
The product owner is responsible, they control the return on investment
The hiring manager is responsible, they hired the developer
The scrum master is accountable, they remove impediments
questions.explanation: The key names the Scrum Team, but the Guide does not assign authority to dismiss or remove employees. Self-management and coaching do not replace an organization's employment policies. Do not infer hiring or firing authority from Scrum accountabilities.
answerText: The scrum team is accountable

questions.prompt: What are two responsibilities of testers in a Scrum Team?
options: Tracking quality metrics
The Developers are responsible for quality
Finding bugs
Verifying the work of Programmers
Scrum has no “tester” role
questions.explanation: Testing specialists working on the Increment are Developers in Scrum. Developers are accountable for quality through the Definition of Done; Scrum defines no separate tester accountability.
answerText: The Developers are responsible for quality
Scrum has no “tester” role

questions.prompt: An organization has decided to adopt Scrum, but management wants to change the terminology to fit with terminology already used. What will likely happen if this is done?
options: Without a new vocabulary as a reminder of the change, very little change may actually happen.
The organization may not understand what has changed with Scrum and the benefits of Scrum may be lost.
Management may feel less anxious.
All of the above.
questions.explanation: Changing labels can hide the changes in accountabilities and practices that adopting Scrum needs. The key treats all listed consequences as possible; these are adoption risks, not guaranteed outcomes.
answerText: All of the above.
expandedAnswer: Without a new vocabulary as a reminder of the change, very little change may actually happen.
The organization may not understand what has changed with Scrum and the benefits of Scrum may be lost.

questions.prompt: What 3 things might a Scrum Product Owner focus on to ensure the product delivers value?
options: Velocity is increasing over time
Direct Customer feedback
How much of the functionality of the product is being utilized
Minimizing changes to project scope
How readily the product can be absorbed and used by its customers
questions.explanation: Customer feedback, usage and adoption inform value decisions. Treat them as evidence to investigate, not automatic proof that every feature creates value.
answerText: Direct Customer feedback
How much of the functionality of the product is being utilized
How readily the product can be absorbed and used by its customers

questions.prompt: True or False: To get started in terms of what to build, Scrum requires no more than a Product Owner with enough ideas for a first sprint, Developers to implement those ideas, and a Scrum Master to help guide the process
options: True
False
questions.explanation: The key emphasizes starting without exhaustive upfront specifications. This shorthand does not waive Scrum's Product Goal, Sprint Goal, Definition of Done or other elements; use it only in that limited sense.
answerText: True

questions.prompt: Who is on the Scrum Team?
options: The Product Owner.
The Scrum Master.
Developers.
Project Manager
None of the above
questions.explanation: A Scrum Team consists of one Product Owner, one Scrum Master and Developers. A project manager is not an additional Scrum accountability.
answerText: The Product Owner.
The Scrum Master.
Developers.

questions.prompt: Who is accountable for creating the most valuable Increment each Sprint?
options: The Scrum Team
The Product Owner
The Scrum Master
The CEO
The Developer
questions.explanation: The whole Scrum Team creates a valuable, useful Increment each Sprint. Distinguish that shared accountability from the Product Owner's accountability for maximizing product value.
answerText: The Scrum Team

summary.title: Learn from evidence
summary.text: Empiricism bases knowledge on experience and decisions on observation. Lean thinking reduces waste. Iterative, incremental work improves predictability and controls risk.

summary.title: Empower the people doing the work
summary.text: Self-managing teams decide internally who does what, when and how. Continuous inspection and adaptation support improvement.

summary.title: Transparency → inspection
summary.text: Make work and its process visible. Important decisions depend on the perceived state of the three artifacts; low transparency makes inspection misleading.

summary.title: Inspection → adaptation
summary.text: Frequently inspect artifacts and progress toward agreed goals. The five events provide a cadence. Inspection should lead to adaptation.

summary.title: Adapt as soon as you learn
summary.text: Adjust unacceptable process or product deviations promptly. Empowerment and self-management enable adaptation. Inspection without adaptation is pointless.

summary.title: Five values guide behavior
summary.text: Commitment · Focus · Openness · Respect · Courage. Practicing the values builds trust and gives life to transparency, inspection and adaptation.

summary.title: One cohesive team · typically ≤10
summary.text: One Product Owner, one Scrum Master and Developers. No sub-teams or hierarchies; the team is cross-functional and self-managing.
summary.qualification: “10 or fewer” is typical, not an absolute limit.

summary.title: Product value / effectiveness / quality
summary.text: Product Owner: maximize product value and manage the backlog effectively. Scrum Master: establish Scrum and enable team effectiveness. Developers: create a plan, uphold quality, adapt daily and hold each other accountable.
summary.qualification: The whole team creates a valuable, useful Increment each Sprint. Product value is more than the amount of work done.

summary.title: One product → shared foundations
summary.text: Multiple Scrum Teams focused on one product share the same Product Goal, Product Backlog and Product Owner. They define and comply with the same Definition of Done.

summary.title: Scaling and event cadence
summary.text: The 2020 Guide does not prescribe identical Sprint schedules for every team. Each team still follows Scrum’s event and Sprint rules.
summary.qualification: The summary’s comparison with SAFe is not established by the Guide. A separate scaling framework may add coordination rules; check that framework directly.

summary.title: Sprint · one month or less
summary.text: The Sprint contains all the work and other events. A new Sprint starts immediately after the previous one. There is no distinct “Sprint 0” in the Guide.
summary.qualification: The summary’s “Spring 0” is a typo. A preparation phase does not waive Scrum’s requirements.

summary.title: Planning · why → what → how
summary.text: The whole Scrum Team collaborates. Why: a valuable Sprint Goal. What: Developers select work through discussion with the Product Owner. How: Developers plan the delivery.
summary.qualification: Maximum 8 hours for a one-month Sprint; usually shorter for shorter Sprints.

summary.title: Daily Scrum · 15 minutes
summary.text: Developers inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the Sprint Backlog every working day. The result is an actionable plan for the next day.
summary.qualification: Yesterday / today / impediments are optional prompts, not three mandatory questions.

summary.title: Review · inspect the outcome
summary.text: The Scrum Team and stakeholders inspect the Sprint outcome and progress toward the Product Goal, then discuss what to do next. It is a working session.
summary.qualification: Maximum 4 hours for a one-month Sprint; usually shorter for shorter Sprints. The Review is not a release gate.

summary.title: Retrospective · improve effectiveness
summary.text: Inspect individuals, interactions, processes, tools and the Definition of Done. Identify the most helpful improvements and address them as soon as possible.
summary.qualification: Maximum 3 hours for a one-month Sprint; usually shorter for shorter Sprints.

summary.title: Artifacts make work and value transparent
summary.text: Each artifact has a commitment that focuses attention and measures progress. These reinforce empiricism and Scrum values.

summary.title: Product Backlog → Product Goal
summary.text: The Product Goal describes a future state of the product. The Product Owner is accountable for developing and explicitly communicating it; the work may be delegated.

summary.title: Sprint Backlog → Sprint Goal
summary.text: The whole Scrum Team creates the Sprint Goal during Sprint Planning. It gives the Sprint a single objective and allows flexibility in the exact work.

summary.title: Increment → Definition of Done
summary.text: An Increment is usable, additive and verified. It meets the Definition of Done. Multiple Increments may be created in a Sprint, and value may be released before its end.
summary.qualification: The summary’s “piece of value per Sprint” must not be read as exactly one Increment, or a mandatory end-of-Sprint release.

summary.title: Who defines Done?
summary.text: Organizational standards apply as a minimum. If none exist, the Scrum Team creates an appropriate Definition of Done. Developers conform to it; teams on one product use the same definition.

summary.title: Inspect Done and improve quality
summary.text: The Retrospective inspects the Definition of Done along with the team’s way of working. Improvements can be made; quality must not decrease during the Sprint.
summary.qualification: The Guide does not say the Retrospective is the only moment the Definition of Done can be improved.

summary.title: Done supports forecasting and transparency
summary.text: Developers use their understanding of Done, past performance and upcoming capacity when selecting work. Done creates a shared understanding of completion and makes quality transparent.

summary.title: Why · the Sprint Goal
summary.text: The whole Scrum Team collaborates on the Sprint Goal. It is finalized before Sprint Planning ends.

summary.title: What · selected backlog items
summary.text: Developers select Product Backlog items through discussion with the Product Owner. The Sprint Backlog is a plan by and for the Developers.
summary.qualification: The summary’s “owned by the entire Scrum Team” blurs shared accountability for the Increment with Developers’ accountability for the plan.

summary.title: How · the delivery plan
summary.text: Developers decide how to turn selected items into a Done Increment. They update the plan throughout the Sprint as they learn.

summarySource.text:
Key elements of the Scrum guide

Fundamentals of Scrum (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9W4RVwsPLLE& )
    Empiricism
    Self-Managed / Empowered Teams
    Continuous Improvement

Pillars (3)
      Transparency
          On the perceived state of the 3 Scrum artifacts.
      Inspection
          Of the Scrum artifacts and progress toward agreed goals
          To help with inspection, Scrum provides cadence in the form of its 5 events.
          Inspection enables adaptation.
      Adaptation
          Inspection without adaptation is considered pointless.
          Adaptation difficult when people involved are not empowered or self-managing.
          A Scrum Team is expected to adapt the moment it learns anything new through inspection.

Artifacts (work, or value), with their commitment (to focus on & to measure progress)
     Product Backlog: Product Goal (defined & communicated by the PO)
     Sprint Backlog: Spring Goal (defined by the whole Scrum Team)
     Increment (Useful piece of value per Sprint) : DOD define by the Scrum Team If not an organizational standard
                                                    Revised during sprint retrospective if needed
The Definition of Done (DOD)
     Guide the Developers on how many Product Backlog items to select for the Sprint.
     Create a shared understanding of when work is complete.
     Increase transparency.

Scrum Values (5) for the scrum team
    Courage
    Focus
    Commitment
    Respect
    Openness

Scrum events (5)
    Sprint: container for all other events (1 month or less. Spring 0 does not exist)
    Sprint Planning (8h max. Why, What, How)
    Daily Scrum (15min could be the 3 questions)
    Sprint Review (4h)
    Sprint Retrospective (3h max)

Sprint Backlog
     Spring Goal: Why (defined by the whole team)
     Selected items: What (“owned” by the entire Scrum Team)
     Tasks / Plan to deliver the increment: How (defined by the dev)

Scrum team
    10 or fewer
    SM
    PO: Optimize the value of the work the Scrum Team does
    Developers

At Scale / multiple scrum team
     Same Product Goal, Product Backlog, and Product Owner, same DOD
     Not mandatory to have the same cadence (not the same as in SAFe)

resources.title: Value is an outcome, not a feature count
resources.text: Test assumptions through experiments and inspect customer outcomes. Use four perspectives: Current Value (benefits today), Unrealized Value (unmet needs), Time-to-Market (delivery responsiveness), and Ability-to-Innovate (capacity to deliver value). Output volume alone does not demonstrate improved customer experience.

resources.title: The Product Owner’s focus
resources.publisher: Scrum.org · What is a Product Owner?
resources.text: Focus on product value and effective backlog management. Work with stakeholders and experiment with ideas; writing stories is only one possible activity. Delegating backlog work does not delegate accountability.

resources.title: Ordering an evolving backlog
resources.publisher: Scrum.org · Introduction to the Product Backlog
resources.text: Ordering balances considerations such as value, risk, return on investment and dependencies. A product has one transparent, evolving backlog; it is not a complete specification fixed upfront.
